# FlutterGuard

> See what ships in your Flutter app. FlutterGuard inspects Flutter Android APKs with an Android app or a source-built CLI that share one JVM detection engine. It reports manifest policy, compiled Dart strings, assets, dependencies, endpoints and signing evidence. No account, no upload, MIT licensed.

- [Canonical site](https://flutterguard.dev/)
- [CLI guide](https://flutterguard.dev/cli/)
- [Google Play listing](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.flutterguard.app)
- [Latest GitHub release](https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/releases/latest)
- [Source (MIT)](https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard)

## Android app

- Discover: FlutterGuard lists the Flutter apps installed on this device, or you pick a single APK.
- Inspect: Read SDK versions, endpoints and exposed strings inside the release.
- Report: Save the evidence on the phone and return to it later.
- The app declares no INTERNET permission. Android 8.0 and newer.

## Distribution and signing

- GitHub releases contain the Android APK and a source-built CLI.
- Google Play is updated separately; its current version is not verified here. Do not assume feature parity between channels.
- Play and GitHub use separate signing channels. Some older GitHub builds used an older key. Moving from one of those builds requires uninstalling the app, which deletes local reports, history and settings. Exporting a report does not restore that history.

## CLI and CI

No published CLI download, Maven package or JitPack artifact is established. Build the launcher from the repository:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard.git
cd FlutterGuard
./gradlew :cli:installDist
export PATH="$PWD/cli/build/install/flutterguard/bin:$PATH"
flutterguard scan INPUT.apk --json OUTPUT.json --sarif OUTPUT.sarif --fail-on confirmed
```

- Requires JDK 17 or newer and the repository's existing Android SDK build setup. The launcher runs the engine on a plain JVM; the scanning machine needs no Android device.
- Output parent directories must exist, and output files must not already exist. The CLI refuses to overwrite and stages new output before an atomic publish.
- Exit 0 is success, 1 is the `--fail-on confirmed` gate, 2 is any argument, input, scan or output error.
- `--json` writes redacted schema `flutterguard/report/2`; secret values are masked. `--sarif` writes SARIF 2.1.0 with APK locations and no source lines.
- GitHub code-scanning ingestion is not verified. Local SARIF validation is not GitHub acceptance.
- The CLI scans one APK. It does not assemble split APKs, decompile Dart, or compare releases. Comparisons exist only in the Android app, for compatible scans of the same package.
- The scan is local. Building may fetch dependencies, and CI artifact uploads follow the workflow's policy.

## Engine

The shared engine is a repository module at https://github.com/anasfik/FlutterGuard/tree/main/engine. It is not a separately published SDK. The Android app and CLI both call it.

## What it reads

- Manifest and package data: package name, version, SDK levels, permissions, exported components, ABIs, backup and debug flags.
- Release contents: bundled SDKs, hosts, endpoints, keys and configuration that shipped in the APK.
- `libapp.so`: strings and symbols inside the AOT machine code.
- Signing data: certificate identity and structural signature facts.
- Route-like strings found in the binary.
- Snapshot metadata describing how the Dart library was built. It is not decompilation and does not definitively prove obfuscation.

## Confidence and grades

Confirmed findings are artifact facts. Suspected matches are leads worth checking. Inventory is listed without a judgement. Only confirmed findings affect the grade. A-F are triage labels, not a security certificate; a confirmed finding does not prove exploitability, credential validity or endpoint reachability.

## Shared limits

- Static analysis is evidence, not proof. A finding is not a confirmed exploit.
- No runtime hooking, traffic interception, authentication testing or live execution.
- `libapp.so` is AOT machine code: strings and symbols, not decompiled Dart.
- Routes are candidate strings, not a navigation graph.
- AABs are not supported; convert with bundletool first.
- Some ROMs block APK reads.
- Scan only apps you own or are authorised to test.
- Uninstalling the Android app deletes private reports and history.

## FAQ

- Is FlutterGuard free? Yes, open source under the MIT licence, no account, no ads, no paid tier.
- Does the Android app need an internet connection? No, it has no INTERNET permission and scans run on the device.
- Does the CLI need an internet connection? The scan is local. Building may download Gradle dependencies, and a CI job may upload artifacts under its own policy.
- Which apps can it check? Flutter apps you own or are authorised to test, installed or supplied as a single APK.
- Does a finding prove the app is exploitable? No, findings are static evidence from the release.
- Where do updates come from? Google Play and GitHub releases; the channels have different versions and signing keys.

## Licence

MIT. Use FlutterGuard only on applications you own or have permission to test. Findings are evidence for your own review, not an authorisation to test third-party apps.

Full detail: [llms-full.txt](https://flutterguard.dev/llms-full.txt)
